assertions.claim: The canonical Stage B surface carries source paths and hashes, contrary to the binding essence-only stage boundary that assigns provenance and integrity metadata outside B.
assertions.proposed_remedy: Remove stage_a_inputs from the canonical essence ledger and retain input hashes only in the authority or generated integrity status.
assertions.falsifier: An Owen-approved ruling explicitly permits top-level source paths and hashes inside the canonical Stage B essence artifact despite the current statement that B carries none.

assertions.claim: The design-target value bundles percentage facts and count facts under one unit of percent, while source_phrase quotes only the counts, so the fields do not have one computable meaning and one complete source shape.
assertions.proposed_remedy: After human confirmation of the intended grain, represent percentage targets and sample/test counts as independently typed values or give every subvalue an explicit unit, and make each source_phrase cover all values carried by its row.
assertions.falsifier: The declared schema assigns units independently to the four value keys and defines source_phrase as allowed to quote only a subset of a row's values.

assertions.quoted_span: "event": "start of a continuous period without detection of the specified pest in the demarcated area on the Article 10 surveys (the establishment, or the last detection)"; "note": "The period restarts at any later detection: the source requires four years of no detection, not four years since establishment; reaching it opens the lifting discretion and does not itself lift."
assertions.claim: The row leaves the alternative start events and reset rule in prose, so Stage C cannot compute the four-year threshold from structured anchor fields without reinterpreting anchor.event and note.
assertions.proposed_remedy: Have a human reread establish a machine-readable resettable-period anchor that distinguishes establishment, last detection and later-detection reset events without asking code to decide their legal meaning.
assertions.falsifier: Stage D already supplies one canonical timestamp named exactly by this composite event, including the legally correct establishment-or-last-detection selection and every later reset, without parsing this prose.

assertions.quoted_span: "expression": "a survey has been carried out at least once during the first year following th", "disposition": "not_a_clock", "ref": null
assertions.claim: The disposition log classifies the expression that mints B-CLK-EU-5(1)(c)-v1-first-year-survey as not_a_clock, contradicting the canonical clock and defeating the claimed expression-grain closure.
assertions.proposed_remedy: Human-reread the disposition population class-wide, collapse overlapping pattern fragments to independently meaningful expressions, and assign each surviving expression the correct clock or parameter reference or a reasoned exclusion.
assertions.falsifier: This disposition fragment denotes a different temporal expression from the clock's verbatim source phrase "at least once during the first year following the identification of the specified pest".

assertions.quoted_span: Confidence and design prevalence stated in the workbook as decimals (e.g. 0.95 / 0.0005); carried in percent so the field has one shape. Planned values; as-run samples and results are Stage D.
assertions.claim: This note carries provenance, normalization rationale and a Stage D allocation rather than a source-stated interaction or genuine open term, contrary to the binding note and essence-only rules; the same note appears on all nine PNI design-target rows.
assertions.proposed_remedy: Remove the repeated row notes and keep any approved normalization convention in the schema authority rather than the essence rows.
assertions.falsifier: The producer source expressly states the normalization-to-percent rule and the Stage D classification quoted by this note.

assertions.claim: generation-status.json is not a pure function of the canonical because its generated map includes every pre-existing CSV in the output directory, including stale or unrelated files the generator neither creates nor removes.
assertions.proposed_remedy: Build the generated hash map from the fixed four projection paths, and separately reject or ignore unrecognized files without allowing ambient directory state into canonical-derived output.
assertions.falsifier: The generated directory is enforced externally as an immutable set containing exactly clocks.csv, parameters.csv, dispositions.csv and closure_manifest.csv before every invocation.

checked_sound: Exhaustive field-shape inventory: all 67 clocks share one ordered field set; anchor has four declared object variants—15 recurrence, 30 legal_state, 20 event and 2 biological—and consequence_on_expiry and completion always use {kind, ref}.

Exhaustive parameter-shape inventory: all 48 parameters share one ordered field set and the same four-key scope shape; actual value variants are 25 scalar strings, 9 {confidence, design_prevalence}, 9 {confidence, design_prevalence, samples, tests}, and 5 year-wrapping month-window objects, with only the mixed-unit design-target variant surviving as drift.
Computability sample—B-CLK-DDS45-eradication-48h: Stage C can take the OPERATOR_RECORD timestamp for execution of vector treatment and add a floor of 48 hours to obtain the earliest removal time.
Computability sample—B-CLK-IT-29(1)-union-entry-5wd: Stage C can take the OFFICIAL_FINDING_CONFIRMED timestamp and add five working days using the Stage D calendar.
Computability sample—B-CLK-EU-6(1)-four-negative-years: Stage C cannot select and reset the anchor without reading prose, as recorded in F3-03.
Computability sample—B-PAR-EU-15(3)-island-exemption-5km: Stage C can compute the island-to-nearest-Union-land distance and apply the structured > 5 km threshold.

Disposition sampling was exhaustive over all eight disposition classes and used a deterministic 20-row sample selected by SHA-256 rank after taking at least two rows per class; every sampled non-null expression was a substring of its Stage A source_quote.

The verifier actually enforces the schema tag, exact row field order, unique row IDs, producer existence, source_phrase containment, inherited intervals, seam range, consumer stable IDs, limited vocabulary checks, note length, anchor key shapes and token existence, event record class, enumerated clock/parameter kinds and units, numeric-string shapes, selected kind-specific constraints, endpoint reference existence, sentinel/silence exclusions, comparator and scope-key presence, disposition producer/class/ref basics, a narrow retrospective-aperture regex, and population-version coverage.

All ten failure classes can still pass scripts/verify_stage_b.py silently: retrospective_aperture can be paraphrased around its narrow regex, while over_provenance, anchor_drift, enum_coercion outside the few hard-coded cases, note_as_repair, population_by_pattern, projection_reading, source_shaped_work, green_gate_closure and phantom_report receive no semantic test; direct human reread is the only gate for their legal meaning.
The read-only verifier passed with 67 clocks, 48 parameters and 761 dispositions, but that result was treated only as bounded mechanical evidence and not semantic acceptance.

Closure is currently honest: all four closure_manifest entries say NOT_ASSERTED, all acceptance_act and semantic_reviewer fields are null, seam 4 is HELD, and generation-status.json says PROJECTION_INTEGRITY_PASS with semantic_acceptance NOT_ASSERTED.

Current projection integrity matches disk: the canonical SHA-256 and all four generated CSV hashes equal generation-status.json, CSV row counts match the canonical arrays, closure IDs cover every clock and parameter exactly, and closure population counts equal population.json for all four seams.

The canonical otherwise contains no per-row hashes, source paths, ASTs, evaluators, evidence bindings, holiday tables or calendar-conversion rules, and the seat binding is recorded once rather than repeated per row.
